title: Handshake, entropy, TLS and browser admission authority
summary: WebSocket owns RFC 6455 handshake/frame validation but not TLS credentials, production entropy, identity or authorization. dev4 keeps wss transport in the owned HTTPS/SocketProvider layer and applies browser-facing Origin/client-key/masking admission at the RFC6455 boundary.
invariants: WebSocketHandshakeCrypto remains the protocol-facing handshake authority contract.
WebSocketMaskSource remains the client frame-mask authority contract.
WebSocketPlatformCrypto.cls is optional and separate from WebSocketAccess.cls.
WebSocketCryptoAuthHandshake uses crypto.auth/0.1 SHA-1 for Sec-WebSocket-Accept and standard base64 encoding.
Production entropy remains behind WebSocketEntropySource and is not claimed qualified by dev4.
TLS certificate, trust and private-key material remain in the owned HTTPS/SocketProvider security authority.
No Socket, BIO, SSL, SSL_CTX or Foreign Runtime object crosses the HTTPS-to-WebSocket handoff.
Browser-facing server admission supports an explicit Origin allowlist, version 13 enforcement, canonical client-key shape and mandatory masked client frames.
HTTPS/mTLS or LDAP identity evidence may be projected to application context but does not become WebSocket authorization automatically.
The RFC 6455 example key/accept vector remains a deterministic contract fixture, not a production randomness mechanism.

provenance.claim: Server-side RFC6455 admission and framing boundary.
